actions: Re-attempted exact artifact recovery for Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.16441066 through public web transport. The peer-reviewed paper and withdrawn ICLR manuscript both still resolve the DOI as the official code location, but the available DOI-to-Zenodo transport would not expose the record file list/checksums in this invocation.
Searched exact title/DOI/citation variants for a non-author rerun. No clear independent exact rerun or failure report was found.

Read the transparent peer-review record. Reviewer 2 explicitly challenged sample-efficiency fairness because baseline C3D/ViViT models lacked equivalent pretraining and requested at least three random seeds. The authors replied that preliminary same-synthetic-task pretraining of C3D/ViViT produced similar or degraded downstream performance, but provided no numerical results for that preliminary control; they also stated that key experiments were repeated across multiple seeds and revised tables/figures report mean±SD.

Performed a reduced source-derived geometry-necessity test rather than another sufficiency constraint. Trained a leaky ReLU recurrent model with tau=2, per-step layer normalization, all-time direction supervision, 12 directions and binary moving-bar sequences. The reduced model used 48 hidden units, 8x8 inputs and T=40 for tractability, not the paper's 512 units/T=100/1e6-episode training.

Identified a 2D direction-coded hidden subspace by least-squares decoding late hidden activity to cos(theta),sin(theta), then orthonormalized the two decoder directions. Class-mean distances in this subspace tracked true circular class distance with Spearman rho=0.932, establishing that the intervention targeted an ordered direction representation rather than arbitrary high-variance PCs.

Scrambled only the recurrent 2x2 operator inside that direction-coded subspace while preserving its singular-value scale; refit only the linear readout on clean data. Compared against equal-Frobenius-norm recurrent scrambles in random 2D residual subspaces. Used eight perturbation seeds and a 1,200-sequence held-out set.

At recurrent perturbation Frobenius norm 0.035, tangent-subspace versus residual-control mean clean-accuracy difference was -0.156 percentage points with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.219,-0.094]; all-gap interpolation difference was -0.740 points, CI [-1.021,-0.437], and tangent perturbation was worse in 7/8 perturbation seeds. Frame-dropout difference was -0.031 points with CI spanning zero. Off-manifold contraction ratio difference also spanned zero.

Repeated at perturbation norm 0.05. Clean-accuracy difference was +0.177 points with CI spanning zero, while all-gap interpolation remained lower by -0.490 points, bootstrap 95% CI [-0.812,-0.156], worse in 7/8 perturbation seeds. Dropout and contraction differences again were not clearly separated.

facts_used: 512-neuron vanilla RNN; tau=2; leaky ReLU recurrence; per-step layer normalization; all-time cross-entropy; Direction task uses T=100, 12 directions and sparse Bernoulli noise p=0.01.
Paper reports Direction manifold effective dimension about 2.11 and recovery from off-manifold perturbation within roughly 5-10 steps.

necessity_test.interpretation: This reduced necessity test gives a small but repeatable signal that recurrent organization specifically inside a direction-coded low-dimensional subspace contributes to robustness against inserted temporally disordered frames even after clean decoding is approximately preserved by readout refitting. The effect did not extend clearly to frame dropout or the off-manifold contraction diagnostic, so it does not establish that the paper's full continuous-attractor geometry is the dominant robustness cause. Because the model, generator, training budget and perturbation are reduced/source-derived rather than exact, this is hypothesis-narrowing evidence only.

evidence_added_this_run: Transparent peer review reveals an unquantified author-side preliminary control: same synthetic pretraining on C3D/ViViT reportedly gave similar or degraded downstream transfer, while reviewers explicitly requested fairer pretraining and multi-seed statistics.

A reduced direction-coded recurrent-subspace necessity intervention preserved clean accuracy to within about two-tenths of a point yet reduced all-gap interpolation robustness by about 0.5-0.74 points relative to equal-norm residual-subspace perturbations across two perturbation magnitudes.
The same intervention did not produce a clear frame-dropout or off-manifold-contraction difference.
candidate_update.interpretation: Primitive isolation plus distributed temporal supervision remains the strongest supported transferable mechanism. There is now a modest necessity signal for task-relevant recurrent subspace organization under temporal interpolation, but not enough to attribute the publication's broader robustness specifically to low-dimensional continuous-attractor geometry.

exact_next_action: Continue exact Zenodo artifact recovery using a route that can expose record files/checksums without importing non-clean state. If still blocked, repeat the necessity intervention on at least three independently trained base RNN seeds at T=100, report direction-subspace smoothness/flow alignment before and after intervention, and use a Jacobian- or tangent-selective recurrent perturbation that matches clean logits more tightly than readout refitting alone. In parallel keep searching public citing work for a non-author rerun. If the multi-base-seed effect does not replicate, downgrade attractor-specific causality further and retain primitive isolation plus all-time temporal supervision as the supported mechanism.
